name: viewer-refresh
title: Desktop viewers: follow the refresh rate of the display the window is on, exactly (59.94, 119.88 on Windows), with the existing FpsCap message
protocol_changes: No wire or capability change: reuses ViewerMessage::FpsCap (protocol.rs:188-191), which every peer accepts, and limits.max_fps at connect. FFI: one new op `{"op":"display_refresh","hz":<f64>}` of the existing pb_mapper_desktop_viewer_call_json export, changed on every side at once (Rust export, Dart DesktopApi interface, implementation, FakeDesktopApi). Windows runner: a `refresh_hz` method on the app's own pb_mapper/desktop_video channel.
design:
Why. (a) The viewer asks for its display's refresh only at connect (and on macOS the fastest screen), so a Smooth session whose window moves from a 120 Hz to a 60 Hz screen keeps encoding, sending and decoding 120 fps of which half are superseded, at half the bits per frame; moving back does not resume 120 without a reconnect. (b) Windows viewers on 1000/1001 modes (59.94, 119.88 Hz: TVs, HDMI timings, some panels) ask 59 or 119 because Flutter reports whole hertz, so a 60/120 Hz host loses about one present a second while content moves: a hitch every second.

Rust (viewer/fps_cap.rs, sink.rs, mod.rs):
1. FpsCap gains `display_fps: Option<u32>` and `display_changed: bool`, set through set_display(fps). ceiling = if fps_override { max_fps } else { min(ceiling_fps(preset), max_fps, display_fps) } (a user-chosen rate ignores the display: the frames are fresher).
2. `release` = display_fps.filter(|d| !fps_override && *d < max_fps).unwrap_or(max_fps): the value meaning 'no backlog cap'. Every place that sends max_fps today sends release instead, including the raise-to-ceiling branch, so a backlog recovery never clears the display limit.
3. On display_changed the next tick sends the new effective value at once, bypassing CAP_CHANGE_MIN, the high-tick gate and the 3 s raise hold: min(backlog cap, display) when lowering, release when no backlog cap; while frozen (paused) it applies at the first tick after resume. Backlog lowering (viewer-fps-cap's capacity logic) keeps working beneath the display ceiling.
4. sink.rs set_display_fps; Viewer::set_display_refresh(hz: f64) rounds and clamps to MIN_VIEWER_FPS..=MAX_FPS as VideoLimits::choose does (Android ignores it, as choose does); session.rs:583-585 already forwards what tick returns. video.rs: a unit test pins 59.94 -> 60 and 119.88 -> 120.
FFI and Dart:
5. ui/native/pb_mapper_ffi/src/desktop/viewer.rs: DisplayRefresh { hz: f64 } op, with its Dart interface (desktop_api.dart), implementation and fake.
6. Windows runner (desktop_video.cpp): WindowRefreshHz(HWND): MonitorFromWindow on the Flutter view's HWND, GetMonitorInfoW for szDevice, QueryDisplayConfig(QDC_ONLY_ACTIVE_PATHS) with DISPLAYCONFIG_DEVICE_INFO_GET_SOURCE_NAME matching viewGdiDeviceName, returning that path's targetInfo.refreshRate exactly; else dmDisplayFrequency. Exposed as `refresh_hz`.
7. New ui/lib/src/ffi/display_refresh.dart: the window's display refresh; on Windows the runner's refresh_hz (bounded at 200 ms, falling back to the current value); elsewhere PlatformDispatcher's view display refreshRate.
8. desktop_store.dart: on macOS, Windows and Linux connect with that refresh as refresh_hz (desktop_store.dart:341, displayMaxHz); a PlatformDispatcher.onMetricsChanged listener (plus window focus and move on Windows) sends display_refresh whenever the value differs from the last sent, and once after connect. Android unchanged.
(The Mac runner's refreshHz stat already reports the window's screen, from viewer-decoder-stats.)
9. Docs: 'Viewer: newest decodable frame, fps cap and recovery' (remote-desktop.md:1643-1683) and the panel's refresh row; CHANGELOG bullet.
verification: Here: `cargo fmt --all`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop fps_cap` and `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --lib video` (lower at once, raise at once, override honoured, backlog lowers beneath the display, a backlog recovery sends release not max_fps; rounding); `cargo test -p pb-mapper-ffi` (op test); `cargo test --workspace --all-features`; `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`. From ui/: `flutter gen-l10n`, `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib test tool`, `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos`, `flutter test` (store test with a fake channel answering 59.94; display_refresh sent on change). CI: android-check (`cargo ndk -t arm64-v8a clippy -p pb-mapper-ffi --locked -- -D warnings`), rust-windows-desktop, macos-app, linux-app; the Windows runner compiles only via release-ui.yml with windows_verify_only; nat-traversal.yml.
measurement: On this Mac: desktop_ui_host with `--fps 120` and the macOS acceptance viewer (maxFps unset, Smooth); mid-run switch the G24H2 from 144 Hz to 60 Hz in System Settings and back: the host's target and pace fall from 120 to 60 within one viewer tick (250 ms) plus a round trip and return to 120; received fps follows; bytes per frame (bitrate / received fps) roughly double at 60; Balanced unchanged. Device: a ProMotion panel with a 60 Hz external; a Windows viewer on a 59.94 or 119.88 Hz mode with a 60 or 120 Hz host on Balanced and Smooth: the panel's max_fps and pace (59 against 60), capture and received fps, desktop_capture_pacing; Windows and Linux per-view display updates. Record under docs/benchmarks/.
verifiable_here: Measure-on-this-Mac for the Rust core, FFI, Dart and the macOS viewer; the Windows runner and Linux behaviour are CI-build and device-only.

name: decoder-install-hints
title: Tell the viewer's user when a better codec is one install away (Windows HEVC Video Extensions, Linux GStreamer decoders)
protocol_changes: None on the wire or FFI. The Windows runner's `decoders` channel reply gains `installable: ["hevc"]` (later "av1").
design:
Why. A Windows viewer whose GPU decodes HEVC (DXVA HEVC Main) but has no HEVC decoder MFT (the Store's HEVC Video Extensions) runs every session on H.264, Baseline from Windows hosts; on this M6's VideoToolbox H.265 reached 43.2 dB at half the bitrate where H.264 reached 35.2 dB on scrolling text (scratchpad notes/dwell.txt), NVENC's gap is smaller but large. A Linux viewer without gst-libav falls back to JPEG at up to 8 FPS. This is phase 1 of R9-win-viewer-d3d11va-hevc-av1 and needs no licensing decision.

1. Windows runner: ProbeDecoders (desktop_video.cpp:307-317) adds `installable: ["hevc"]` when HevcLimit(adapter) is non-null but SyncDecoders(MFVideoFormat_HEVC) is empty (av1-viewers adds "av1" when Av1Limit is non-null and no AV1 MFT is registered).
2. Linux: derived in Dart from the existing `decoders` reply (desktop_video.cc:148-169): h264 null means the base decoders are missing (JPEG fallback); h265 null means no hardware H.265. No runner or module change.
3. Dart: DesktopDecoders gains `installable` and `missing`. The codec menu (viewer_menus.dart) and the quality panel show, only while the session is on H.264 or JPEG and the codec preference is Auto: on Windows a one-line hint with a button opening the Microsoft Store page of HEVC Video Extensions (verify the product ID when implementing); on Linux the package list from docs/user-guide.md:415 with a link to the guide. Dismissible per device (viewer_prefs.dart). New .arb strings in both languages, then gen-l10n.
4. Docs: the user-guide pair (English and Chinese together) mention the hint; CHANGELOG bullet.
verification: Here, from ui/: `flutter gen-l10n` (l10n_untranslated.json stays {}), `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib test tool`, `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos`, `flutter test` (DesktopDecoders parsing; the hint shows only for Auto on H.264 or JPEG; dismissal persists); icons from AppIcons. CI: linux-app, flutter-syntax-check; the Windows runner compiles only via release-ui.yml with windows_verify_only.
measurement: Device: a Windows PC with an HEVC-capable GPU and no extension shows the hint; after installing, the probe reports h265 and the quality panel shows H.265 (record sent bits per frame and a PSNR-comparable screenshot before and after); a Linux box without gst-libav shows the package hint and, after installing, decodes H.264 at the session's pace.
verifiable_here: Dart logic build-and-test here; runners CI-build only; the effect depends on the user acting (device).

name: viewer-scroll
title: Scrolling: one wheel notch is one host notch on every viewer, high-resolution (1/120-notch) scrolling by capability, and trackpad momentum carried to the host
protocol_changes: Desktop wire, ALPN unchanged: host capability `wheel_hires` (from a new BackendCaps.hires_wheel, listed in BackendCaps::values()); new `Input::Scroll { horizontal: i32, vertical: i32, continuous: bool }` in 1/120-notch units (continuous serde default, skipped when false), |v| <= 12000 in Input::validate, sent only to a host that listed wheel_hires (Viewer::input returns NotOffered otherwise). Helper pipe: Input::Scroll crosses it and StartCaps gains hires_wheel: bump HELPER_PROTOCOL to one above master's value at merge with both pipe names (.v<n>). No FFI export change (the existing input op carries Input JSON). Runner channel pb_mapper/desktop_pointer gains `wheel_lines` (Windows).
design:
Why. (a) remote_surface.dart turns every PointerScrollEvent into notches at kWheelPxPerNotch = 30 logical px (:19, :229-238), but each embedder reports one wheel notch as a different distance: Windows lines x 100/3 physical px (flutter_window.cc:468-478, 798-808; flutter_windows_view.cc:660-661), i.e. 100/DPR logical at 3 lines; macOS 40 logical per line (FlutterViewController.mm:735-757); Linux 53 (fl_scrolling_manager.cc:108). One Windows notch at 100% sends 3,3,4,3 notches (9-12 lines on a Windows host); macOS and Linux send 1,1,2 and 2,2,1 patterns. (b) A 30 px trackpad move becomes a whole notch: 3 lines (about 100 px) on a Windows host, 1 line on a Mac host, so remote content jumps in steps and scrolls about 3x too fast on Windows hosts. (c) Flutter drops OS scroll momentum on every desktop platform (macOS skips momentum-phase events, FlutterViewController.mm:614-625; Windows suppresses DirectManipulation inertia, direct_manipulation.cc:73, 152; GTK/libinput produce none), and pb-mapper reads raw PanZoom in a Listener (remote_surface.dart:213-226), so a fling stops dead on the remote computer. airhand forwards OS momentum as wheel events (client/src/lib/input.ts:518-530).

1. Notch fidelity (R4-wheel-notch-fidelity; every host, old ones included, no protocol): for a mouse-kind PointerScrollEvent, notches = delta / pxPerNotch with pxPerNotch per viewer platform: Windows 100 x lines/3 / devicePixelRatio, macOS 40, Linux 53; the carry stays. `lines` comes from `wheel_lines` on the Windows runner's pb_mapper/desktop_pointer channel (SPI_GETWHEELSCROLLLINES; 3 if the call fails). Trackpad PanZoom and trackpad-kind scroll keep their own distance per notch.
2. Units (R4-hires-scroll): 120 = one notch = 100 logical px of continuous travel. Protocol as above; Outbound::submit sums a single-Scroll batch onto a tail Scroll of the same generation and continuity (beside outbound.rs:249-261), so a trackpad flood never fills the 512-event queue.
3. Dart _wheelBy, when capabilities contain wheel_hires: PointerPanZoomUpdate and trackpad-kind PointerScrollEvent -> units = px x 1.2, continuous; a mouse PointerScrollEvent -> units = notches x 120 (notches per step 1), continuous = false; a carry per axis. Without the capability send today's notches at the corrected per-platform notch size.
4. Host: Injector::scroll(h, v, continuous) has a default that accumulates whole notches into wheel(); native.rs maps Scroll; thread C re-aims the pointer before Scroll as before Wheel (worker/control.rs:458-470). Windows: one SendInput carrying MOUSEEVENTF_WHEEL mouseData = -vertical and/or MOUSEEVENTF_HWHEEL mouseData = horizontal (only the nonzero ones). macOS: continuous posts CGScrollEventUnit::Pixel with px = units / 1.2 (points) with a carry and kCGScrollWheelEventIsContinuous = 1; discrete stays CGScrollEventUnit::Line at units/120 lines with a carry (one line per notch as today). The synthetic backend lists the capability so desktop_ui_host logs Scroll.
5. Momentum (R4-trackpad-momentum), Dart in RemoteSurface: track PanZoomUpdate pan deltas with a VelocityTracker (trackpad kind, event timestamps); on PointerPanZoomEnd above kMinFlingVelocity run a Ticker-driven decay with the viewer platform's physics (macOS's 0.998/ms deceleration as BouncingScrollSimulation's friction; a ClampingScrollSimulation-like curve on Windows and Linux); each tick sends the integrated delta through _wheelBy (continuous Scroll units with wheel_hires, else notches with the carry). Cancel on PointerScrollInertiaCancelEvent, a new PanZoomStart, a pointer down, a discrete wheel event, focus or control loss, or a generation change. Outbound summing bounds the queue.
6. Helper: bump as above, one record of the bump in the remote-desktop.md protocol history.
7. Docs and CHANGELOG: the Platforms table (remote-desktop.md:1132), the Constants Input row, the 'a notch per 30 px' text (:237-238); the user-guide pair if it mentions scrolling or the helper update.
Legacy guard: if a classic Win32 listbox or a Java Swing list fails to scroll under continuous input on a device, add a viewer setting to turn smooth scroll off.
verification: Here: `cargo fmt --all`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-features` (serde and validation; Outbound summing; pure functions for the Windows sign and the macOS pixel/line carry; a viewer refusing Scroll to an older host; a helper-protocol round trip of Input::Scroll and StartCaps.hires_wheel; readiness tests for the new protocol number), `cargo test --workspace --all-features`; `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`; `cargo run -p pb-mapper --features desktop --example desktop_loopback`. From ui/: `flutter gen-l10n`, `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib test tool`, `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos`, `flutter test` (conversion per target platform with debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride for Windows at DPR 1, 1.5, 2, macOS and Linux: one notch event yields exactly one host notch; capability gating; momentum decay, distance within platform bounds and every cancellation). CI rust-windows-desktop, rust-macos-desktop, linux-app, macos-app, flutter-syntax-check, nat-traversal.yml; the Windows runner via release-ui.yml windows_verify_only.
measurement: On this Mac, the macOS viewer against `cargo run -p pb-mapper --features desktop --example desktop_ui_host -- --clip clip.h264 --dir target/desktop-ui`: host_input shows one Scroll per trackpad event, continuous=true, about 1.2 units per logical px (a 300 px swipe sums to about 360); a mouse-wheel notch sums to exactly +-120 (before: 1-2 notches per notch, 1,1,2 pattern); after a fast two-finger swipe a decaying series of Scroll events for about 1 s after PanZoomEnd (before: none), and a second touch stops it within one event. Device: Windows host with an owned Tk or Win32 fixture logging WM_MOUSEWHEEL count and delta while a Mac viewer scrolls 300 px on its trackpad (before about 10 notches of 120 in bursts, after many small deltas); a Windows viewer at 100% and 150% against that logger (before 3-4 x 120 per physical notch, after 1 x 120); a classic Win32 listbox and a Java Swing list still scroll; a macOS host (Accessibility) with an NSView logging scrollWheel deltaY, hasPreciseScrollingDeltas and isContinuous; Windows and Linux touchpad momentum. No data-path benchmark is needed (input lane only).
verifiable_here: Build-and-test on this Mac (Rust, Dart, the macOS viewer against desktop_ui_host); Windows and Linux runners CI-build only; host-side effects device-only.

name: relative-pointer
title: Relative pointer mode with pointer lock for apps that hide and recenter the host pointer (games, 3D viewports)
protocol_changes: Desktop wire, ALPN unchanged: host capability `relative_pointer` (from BackendCaps.relative_pointer, Windows and macOS injectors and the synthetic backend); `Input::MoveBy { dx: i32, dy: i32 }` with |d| <= 4096, sent only to a host that listed it (Viewer::input NotOffered otherwise). Helper pipe: Input::MoveBy and StartCaps.relative_pointer cross it: bump HELPER_PROTOCOL to one above master's value at merge with both pipe names. Runner channel pb_mapper/desktop_pointer gains lock/unlock and posts raw deltas. No FFI export change.
design:
Why. Raw-input games and 3D viewports on a Windows host get no motion at all (SetCursorPos is not input), and apps that hide and recenter the pointer (FPS cameras, Blender or CAD orbit with continuous grab) fight absolute moves on both hosts: the view jumps or stops at the picture's edge. airhand switches to relative moves with pointer lock (client/src/lib/input.ts:1-40; crates/airhand-proto session.rs:30-55; host/input/macos.rs:236-243).

1. Protocol and host: capability and Input::MoveBy as above; Outbound::submit sums a single MoveBy onto a tail MoveBy (outbound.rs:249-261). Injector::pointer_by: Windows relative SendInput MOUSEEVENTF_MOVE (the OS pointer follows speed and precision settings; raw-input readers get exact deltas); macOS MouseMoved (Dragged while a button is held) at the current location plus the delta with MouseEventDeltaX/Y set and the injector's cached position cleared, as airhand host/input/macos.rs:236-243. native.rs maps MoveBy; thread C records no injected echo for it and starts the 2 ms hot cursor sample after MoveBy (pointer-cadence's shape_due extended to positions) so the painted pointer follows within about 2 ms. WinCursor::read reports a null hCursor as hidden (pure function test).
2. Dart: DesktopStore.send sums MoveBy into the pending slot within the 4 ms gate; NOT_FRESH drops MoveBy rather than keeping it. In relative mode the viewer takes every cursor report (no cursor_sequence set-aside); RemoteCursorLayer paints the host pointer; the OS pointer is hidden and locked.
3. Modes (airhand input.ts:1-40), a per-device preference in viewer_prefs.dart and the viewer menu: auto (lock when the host reports the pointer hidden while a button is held, or hidden through 300 ms of movement; unlock when it shows and every button is up; Windows' hide-while-typing never locks because a pointer reappearing within 300 ms does not count); desktop (never lock); game (always lock). A 1 s Esc hold releases the lock, and so does focus loss.
4. Runners (desktop_pointer files from native-cursor), each accumulating raw deltas and posting them at most once per loop turn: Windows ClipCursor to the picture, ShowCursor(FALSE), RegisterRawInputDevices on the top-level window for relative WM_INPUT (handled from flutter_window.cpp's message hook); macOS CGAssociateMouseAndMouseCursorPosition(false), NSCursor.hide, an NSEvent local monitor reading deltaX/deltaY; Linux X11 gdk_seat_grab with XInput2 XI_RawMotion (adds libxi-dev), Linux Wayland zwp_locked_pointer_v1 with zwp_relative_pointer_v1, code generated by wayland-scanner in CMake (adds wayland-protocols to the linux-app CI job). Every lock path restores association and visibility on unlock, dispose and focus loss.
5. Docs: input section and capability list, the user-guide pair (modes; helper update); CHANGELOG bullet. Keep capability lists within MAX_CAPABILITIES.
verification: Here: `cargo fmt --all`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-features` (serde, validation, Outbound summing, a viewer refusing MoveBy to an older host, a helper-protocol round trip, the null-hCursor rule), `cargo test --workspace --all-features`; `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`; `cargo run -p pb-mapper --features desktop --example desktop_loopback`. From ui/: `flutter gen-l10n` (untranslated stays {}), `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib test tool`, `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos`, `flutter test` (auto-lock rules including hide-while-typing, MoveBy summing in the gate, the NOT_FRESH drop, Esc hold, focus loss); icons from AppIcons. macOS app build here. CI rust-windows-desktop, rust-macos-desktop, linux-app (`flutter build linux --debug`, `bash scripts/build/check-linux-bundle.sh ui/build/linux/x64/debug/bundle`, `bash scripts/test/linux-desktop-video.sh --software`), macos-app, ios-app, flutter-syntax-check, nat-traversal.yml; Windows runner via release-ui.yml windows_verify_only.
measurement: On this Mac, the macOS viewer against desktop_ui_host with relative_pointer listed by the synthetic backend: in game mode host_input logs MoveBy deltas while the local pointer stays locked and hidden, and an Esc hold restores it. Device: a raw-input fixture and Blender orbit with continuous grab on a Windows host, driven from Mac, Windows and Linux viewers: WM_INPUT relative deltas arrive (0 today) and the view rotates without jumps; a Mac host in game mode with a 3D app; ordinary desktop use unchanged in auto mode.
verifiable_here: Build-and-test on this Mac (Rust, Dart, macOS viewer against desktop_ui_host); Windows and Linux runners CI-build; host behaviour device-only.

name: mac-vt-padded-capture
title: Mac host: capture unaligned sizes into a 16-padded surface and crop them in the SPS, so VideoToolbox takes its fast path at every size
protocol_changes: None: H.264 and HEVC carry the visible size in the SPS (frame_cropping / conformance_window), which every viewer's decoder already honours (every 1920x1080 stream today is coded 1088 and cropped). VideoFormat.width/height keep meaning the content size.
design:
Why. VideoToolbox encodes a 16-unaligned picture through an internal copy. Measured here with synthetic surfaces, padded against unpadded at the native size, 60 fps dwell p50: 3024x1964 12.15/11.90 -> 10.93/10.80 ms; 1920x1080 5.04/5.98 -> 4.30/4.35 ms; at pace 120, 3024x1964 unaligned runs at 19 ms dwell with two in flight against about 11 ms aligned at the same ~90 fps (scratchpad notes r2rev_ext.txt, r2rev_align.txt). These are the commonest Mac hosts at the default Native limit: MacBook Pro 14 (3024x1964), MacBook Air 13 (2940x1912), 1920x1080 externals, and scaled sizes keep their exact aspect. kVTCompressionPropertyKey_CleanAperture does not write the crop (re-parsed SPS stays 1088/1968; scratchpad r2rev_clap.txt), so the host rewrites it.

Phase 0 (gate): read the device trace mac-vt-submit-thread added (CVPixelBufferGetExtendedPixels, plane heights and bytes per row, IOSurfaceGetAllocSize at the first picture). If ScreenCaptureKit's surfaces already declare 16-padding, stop and record the result: this item then has no effect.

Phase 1:
1. Sizes, in MacVideo::open: content = scaled_size(...) exactly; coded = each dimension rounded up to a multiple of 16.
2. ScreenCaptureKit (capture.rs configuration): width and height = coded; destinationRect = (0, 0, content) (macOS 12.3+), so the display is written 1:1, or scaled as today, into the top-left; with preservesAspectRatio false (from mac-capture-cadence) it fills that rect exactly; the remainder takes the configured opaque black background.
3. Encoder: the VideoToolbox session is created at the coded size; VideoFormat.width/height report the content size.
4. codec/sps.rs (created by win-encoder-settings for H.264): add the HEVC SPS parser (profile_tier_level with sub-layers, chroma_format_idc, picture size) and writers: H.264 frame_cropping_flag = 1 with right and bottom offsets in CropUnit 2 for 4:2:0 frame-only streams, HEVC conformance_window_flag with conf_win_right/bottom_offset in units of 2, copying every remaining bit (VUI included).
5. Output path (encoder.rs): rewrite the parameter sets once per CMFormatDescription, cached by its pointer, so only keyframes carry them and nothing runs per packet; they go to annex_b (encoder.rs:706-717).
6. Fallback: a parse failure at the first keyframe sets padding off for the process and fails the session once; the rebuild uses today's exact size.
7. Input and cursor mapping use display geometry and a proportional picture, so they stay exact.
8. Docs: the Mac paragraph and 'H.265 and H.264'; CHANGELOG bullet with measured dwell.
(This supersedes R2-vt-align-scaled-size, dropped: rounding the content size down distorts the aspect by up to 0.8% and covers scaled sizes only.)
verification: Here: `cargo fmt --all`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-features`: sps tests on VideoToolbox-made parameter sets for H.264 (Constrained High and High) and HEVC Main at 1920x1088, 3024x1968 and 3344x2160, re-parsed with CMVideoFormatDescriptionCreateFromH264ParameterSets/HEVCParameterSets to 1920x1080, 3024x1964 and 3340x2160; an ignored test encoding a padded picture with a marker row at the content's last line, decoding with VTDecompressionSession (objc2-video-toolbox decode feature for tests only) and asserting the output size and the marker. `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`; `cargo run -p pb-mapper --features desktop --example desktop_loopback`. CI rust-macos-desktop and nat-traversal.yml.
measurement: Here: an ignored dwell A/B, padded at the coded size against unpadded at the content size, pre-painted ring, 5 alternating rounds, pace 60 and 120, both codecs: `cargo test --release -p pb-mapper-desktop --lib -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1 video_toolbox_padded`. Pass: dwell p50 lower by >= 1 ms at the 1440p- and 4K-class sizes; equal units/s. Device: the Phase 0 trace first; then a MacBook Pro 14 host at Native: encoder_dwell_ms before and after; on a Windows, Mac, Linux and Android viewer no extra rows or columns, clicks land at the edges. Record under docs/benchmarks/.
verifiable_here: The SPS rewrite and VideoToolbox encode and decode are verifiable here; ScreenCaptureKit's padding and destinationRect behaviour is device-only.

name: encoder-throughput-cap
title: Cap the pace at the encoder's measured throughput when units queue four deep, so dwell falls back to one or two service times
protocol_changes: None. The pace Stats already report reflects the cap. No helper field (see design).
design:
Why. When a Media Foundation encoder is slower than the pace and serial at its bottleneck while still accepting input, four units queue and each waits behind three: an 11 ms encoder at pace 120 has about 44 ms dwell, uneven. Capping the pace at what it delivers gives 11-16 ms with even spacing. NVIDIA is unaffected (3.1 ms at 4K); AMD and Intel at 4K or 1440p 120 are unmeasured, so how often this triggers is shown by its trace. Mac hosts are covered by their submit thread's two-in-flight gate and the H.265 standard-RC switch.

Simplified from the proposal: no Backend::encoder_full and no helper `full` field. After win-mf-output-events, Submit::Full means only MAX_IN_FLIGHT (= ENCODER_DEPTH, which thread C already sees as pending_video() >= ENCODER_DEPTH) or a rare empty sample allocator; the serial-before-NeedInput case is Submit::Waiting, which keeps the tick armed and builds no queue.
1. worker/window.rs counts full ticks per second (ticks where pending_video() >= ENCODER_DEPTH), apart from transport skips, with units produced and dwell p50.
2. Rule: full ticks >= max(2, pace/10) in a second set cap = max(the preset's min_fps, floor(0.95 x units)); after 3 s without a full tick the cap rises by max(1, cap/20); it clears at the QoS pace.
3. Apply it in capture_step's min pace (worker/capture.rs) and publish it as an AtomicU32 in each slot's SessionShared (shared.rs) that the session hands to its Qos (session.rs), whose pace() takes min with it (qos.rs, like viewer_cap at qos.rs:590-597).
4. Pipelined guard: keep the dwell p50 of the second before capping; if 2 s after capping dwell p50 is not below 0.6x of it, lift the cap and do not cap again for 30 s (latency, not throughput, filled the queue).
5. Trace `desktop_encoder_cap` {cap, full_ticks, units, dwell_before, dwell_after}.
6. Docs: the pacing paragraph and Diagnostics; CHANGELOG bullet only with device evidence of a vendor that triggers it.

name: host-direct-bbr
title: BBR on the desktop host's direct QUIC (the video sender), once receipt-driven control owns the rate
protocol_changes: None on the wire (congestion control is sender-local). No public RegisterOptions field: a #[doc(hidden)] Client method; no Node, CLI or helper-pipe change.
design:
Why. On WAN direct paths with random loss of about 0.1% or more and RTTs of 50 ms or more (cross-border links, cellular hotspots, long-haul paths), Cubic's loss response caps the video sender's throughput and slows IDRs and scroll bursts. BBR is not limited by random loss. Nothing changes on LAN or clean paths. On policed uplinks only receipt control protects the path, hence the ship order.

1. A #[doc(hidden)] Client method, e.g. `register_with_sender_congestion(request, options, SenderCongestion::Bbr)`, threading a crate-private choice through DirectPolicy (direct_policy.rs:17-24) to the provider Network::new (direct/provider.rs:301), identity.server and transport(), which sets congestion_controller_factory(Arc::new(quinn::congestion::BbrConfig::default())). pb-mapper-desktop's host.rs:383 calls it, compiled in, so the Windows background host needs no helper-pipe field.
2. The consumer side, generic tunnels and the relay QUIC carrier stay on Cubic.
3. DirectLink (non_exhaustive) gains a controller label so device traces tell the two apart.
4. pb-mapper-testkit: new lossy_udp(loss, delay, rate_bps): a per-direction ordered queue after airhand crates/airhand-link/src/lib.rs:85-150, with a seeded PRNG and raised socket buffers; test-only (its per-packet copies never reach a data path).
5. New example crates/pb-mapper-desktop/examples/direct_cc_bench.rs: two quinn endpoints with pb-mapper's direct TransportConfig through the forwarder; 60 fps P-frames of 8.3 KB and a 150 KB IDR every 2 s under the credit window, with echoed receipts.
6. Ship only if the bench gates below pass; otherwise keep Cubic and record why.
7. Docs: transport section (sender congestion control); CHANGELOG bullet.
verification: Here: `cargo fmt --all`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test -p pb-mapper-client -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-features`, `cargo test -p pb-mapper-cli --all-features --test e2e direct`, `cargo test --workspace --all-features`; `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`; `cargo run -p pb-mapper --features desktop --example desktop_loopback`. CI nat-traversal.yml on Linux (`cargo build -p pb-mapper-cli --features port-mapping`, `sudo python3 scripts/test_nat_traversal.py --binary target/debug/pb-mapper`), rust-windows-desktop, node-e2e.
measurement: On this Mac, release: `cargo run --release -p pb-mapper-desktop --example direct_cc_bench` over RTT {20, 60, 120 ms} x loss {0, 0.1, 1%} x policer {none, 5 Mbit/s}, Cubic against BBR: frame and IDR latency p50/p95/p99, delivered Mbit/s for 4 and 8 Mbit/s app-limited video (the Mathis check), lost_packets and congestion_events from LinkStats; then a closed-loop slow_link variant over such a quinn connection, 3 release runs each. Ship only if IDR p95 falls and delivered rate rises at 0.1-1% loss, and in the policer case p99 frame latency and loss do not rise with receipt control on. name: standby-session
title: A warm standby session on the other path: survive a dead direct path in about 1.5 s and upgrade a relayed session to direct
protocol_changes: Desktop wire, ALPN unchanged: capability `standby` both ways; optional `Accepted.ticket` (32 bytes from ring's SystemRandom, base64url) and `Authenticate.standby_for`, each sent only to a peer that listed the capability (serde default, omitted when unset). No relay wire or DIRECT_VERSION change. SDK: a #[doc(hidden)] `Client::connect_tcp_direct` (no PathPolicy variant, no ConnectOptions field). No FFI or Dart change (logic inside Viewer); no helper-pipe change (HostStatus keeps its shape).
design:
Why. A direct-specific failure (a NAT rebinding or firewall that kills the punched path while the relay is alive) costs an estimated 8-9 s outage today, with the room emptying and display modes restored in between; a relayed session that fell back transiently stays on the relay for its life (the deployed TCP relay measured a 194 ms median ping, docs/remote-desktop.md:2533). Two ordinary sessions, no splice, no new ALPN.

1. When standbys open. A relay standby opens only for an internet-direct primary (punched or port-mapped QUIC), never for LAN QUIC or LAN TCP. A direct-only standby opens only after a NegotiationTimeout, NegotiationFailed or Unreachable fallback; it obeys the shared cooldown (direct-cooldown) and the NetworkHints generation, is never tried after NotOffered, reuses one Consumer and Network per Viewer across attempts, and records its own outcome (it must not log session_path_selected path=relay or count as a fallback).
2. Protocol as above.
3. Host acceptor: check the token first in constant time, then the ticket in constant time over SHA-256 digests. A standby takes a standby permit (one per active slot), starts paused, causes no room keyframe, and does not appear in HostStatus or in peer cursors.
4. Promotion is a Resume on the standby. Under the room lock the room moves display-mode ownership, the admission lease and the ticket to the promoted slot, then ends the primary with End::Closed. Held input is released at the primary's end, failing closed. The resume IDR is forced; reset_baseline runs only if the route differs. Restore runs when the pair ends.
5. Viewer, new viewer/standby.rs: promote at once on a transport error on the primary, or when the primary has had no bytes for max(1.5 s, 4 x base RTT) while the standby received at least one message in that interval; promote a committed direct standby at once (default order, no RTT gate). Attach the standby to the VideoSink with a discontinuity so it waits for the IDR (sink.rs:377-386), then swap the metrics connection slot; document that an earlier subscribe_metrics stream ends at a switch.
6. Telemetry, trace only: desktop_viewer_promoted{cause, outage_ms}, desktop_viewer_standby{route, outcome}.
7. Established direct sessions keep belonging to the endpoints: coordinator loss, revocation or relay rejection never close them (CLAUDE.md invariants unchanged).
8. Docs: the user-guide pair, the remote-desktop.md lifecycle and constants, a relay operator note (one extra relay stream per internet-direct viewer); CHANGELOG bullet. Keep each capability list within MAX_CAPABILITIES.
verification: Here: `cargo fmt --all`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop -p pb-mapper-client --all-features` including tests/session.rs (host: a standby takes no slot and causes no IDR; a wrong ticket gets Denied and over the limit Busy; promotion ends the primary; display-mode ownership moves; no restore on promotion), then `cargo test --workspace --all-features` and `cargo test -p pb-mapper-cli --all-features --test e2e direct`; `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`; `cargo run -p pb-mapper --features desktop --example desktop_loopback`. CI: rust-windows-desktop, rust-macos-desktop, android-check, node-e2e (SDK surface compiled), nat-traversal.yml on Linux (`cargo build -p pb-mapper-cli --features port-mapping`, `sudo python3 scripts/test_nat_traversal.py --binary target/debug/pb-mapper`).
measurement: In-process on this Mac: testkit Shape gains `blocked: AtomicBool`, which holds every byte; a slow_link-style rig opens the primary through shaped link A and the standby through link B (a cfg(test) hook picks the standby's relay address; both relay-only, so blocking A emulates a failure specific to the primary's path). Block A at t = 6 s: time from the block to the first presented frame of the promoted session (sink snapshot), keyframe count, time until control is granted again; 10 runs. Baseline at master: the same rig without a standby, block -> session ended plus a timed Viewer::connect -> first frame. Upgrade: pb-mapper-testkit Relay::start_with_direct with loopback direct and a cfg(test) fault failing the first prepare then released: time to Route::Direct, exactly one IDR, no frozen interval over 300 ms. Release: `cargo test --release -p pb-mapper-desktop --lib -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1 slow_link`. Device: a Windows host and macOS, Windows and Linux viewers across two real NATs; a host firewall rule drops UDP mid-session; separately UDP blocked for the first 5 s then the upgrade watched. Record under docs/benchmarks/.

name: linux-video-plane
title: Linux viewer: present video on a GTK GL plane under a transparent FlView, off Flutter's fixed 60 Hz clock
protocol_changes: None on the wire, FFI or module ABI. The runner channel `pb_mapper/desktop_video`: the create reply gains `plane`, a new `place` method, `grey` implemented for the plane, and stats gain planeIntervalP50Ms/P95Ms and refreshIntervalMs. The Dart DesktopVideoTexture interface and its fakes change with it.
design:
Why. Every Linux viewer presents at most 60 fps through Flutter's fixed timer (proven from the pinned 3.44.9 sources); each picture waits for that timer, unsynchronised with the display (mean about 8 ms), then raster, populate and compose, then GTK's frame clock. With a plane: 120 Hz+ monitors on Smooth get up to 120 fps on Wayland (GNOME, KDE, wlroots) and Mutter X11; every user loses one unsynchronised wait plus 1-4 ms of Flutter work (estimate 8-13 ms off the mean at 60 Hz); on X11 a video picture no longer triggers a full-window glReadPixels.

1. Runner (my_application.cc:59-78): the FlView becomes the overlay child of a GtkOverlay whose main child is a new PbVideoPlane, a GtkGLArea in ui/linux/runner/desktop_video_plane.cc (has-alpha FALSE, auto-render). The plane starts hidden and the FlView background stays opaque black. Only while a plane-backed viewer has placed a visible rect: show the plane and fl_view_set_background_color(#00000000) (takes effect on the next draw, fl_view.cc:862-867); revert on visible=false or dispose. Outside a session nothing changes.
2. UI thread: fl_dart_project_set_ui_thread_policy(project, FL_UI_THREAD_POLICY_RUN_ON_SEPARATE_THREAD) (public in 3.44.9, fl_dart_project.cc:121) as its own commit, measured A/B; keep it only if the plane's p95 interval improves under Dart load.
3. Plane render (GTK thread): if a new picture is pending, acquire it through module->acquire (the receipt) and convert it with linux-gpu-convert's GL helper into an RGBA8 texture in GDK's context (EGL on Wayland, so dma-buf import works; GLX on X11, the YUV-upload path, reporting 'no dma-buf' to the module for this presenter); draw one quad into the placed rect with a scissor to the clip (GLSL 150 core, or ES 1.00 when gdk_gl_context_get_use_es); keep the last RGBA texture so a redraw caused by FlView or an overlay never re-acquires or re-converts. In plane mode frame_ready never calls fl_texture_registrar_mark_texture_frame_available: it sets an atomic pending flag and once per pending picture g_main_context_invoke_full(G_PRIORITY_HIGH) runs gtk_widget_queue_draw_area on the placed rect.
4. Stall fallback: a picture pending 100 ms with no plane render is acquired by a GTK timeout (the receipt) without drawing and kept for the next paint (well under the 700 ms watchdog; keeps receipts when a Wayland window is covered).
5. Grey still: implement `grey` (the DesktopVideoTexture method mac-viewer-layer added) as a saturation matrix uniform in the plane's shader; GreyStill already calls it for native presenters (extend its condition to `plane`).
6. Dart hole: viewer_stage.dart:185-197 draws a NativeVideoHole (new native_video_hole.dart) instead of Texture when picture.plane is set: a leaf render object with isRepaintBoundary true; its paint calls context.setWillChangeHint() (never raster-cached) and draws the picture rect intersected with the stage clip with BlendMode.clear, clearing the ground desktop_viewer.dart:275 and touch_viewer.dart:397 painted; the cursors and overlays paint after it as today. From paint it computes getTransformTo(null) x size x devicePixelRatio (GDK's integer scale) and, when that or the clip changes, sends `place` {textureId, visible, x, y, w, h, clipX, clipY, clipW, clipH} after the frame; it sends visible=false when it was not painted in a frame, including route transitions drawn inside an OpacityLayer.
7. Channel: create answers {textureId, plane}; the plane goes to the first texture only, only if the GtkGLArea realized with no gtk_gl_area_get_error, never under FLUTTER_LINUX_RENDERER=software; every refusal stays on the Flutter texture. dispose hides the plane and restores the opaque background. DesktopVideoTexture gains place(); the channel texture and test fakes change in the same commit.
8. Stats: planeIntervalP50Ms/P95Ms from gdk_frame_clock_get_timings (presentation_time, or frame_time where absent) and refreshIntervalMs from gdk_frame_clock_get_refresh_info.
9. Upgrade note in the docs: when the Flutter pin moves to 3.50+ (Wayland subsurface renderer, X11 fl_opengl_frame), re-verify that Flutter's subsurface buffer keeps alpha over the plane before shipping.
10. Docs: 'The app's video path' and 'macOS, iOS and Linux decoders' (2204-2266); CHANGELOG bullet.
verification: Here, from ui/: `flutter gen-l10n`, `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib test tool`, `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos`, `flutter test` (NativeVideoHole paints with BlendMode.clear, sets the will-change hint, sends place and visible=false at the right frames; fakes keep the Texture). CI linux-app: `flutter build linux --debug`, `bash scripts/build/check-linux-bundle.sh ui/build/linux/x64/debug/bundle`, `bash scripts/test/linux-desktop-video.sh --software`. CI macos-app and flutter-syntax-check for the shared Dart.
measurement: Device-only, before and after, on an Intel iGPU and an NVIDIA desktop; GNOME Wayland, KDE Wayland, GNOME X11 and Xfce X11; 60 Hz and 144 Hz monitors: ui/tool/desktop_viewer_acceptance.dart at 1080p with Balanced and Smooth (maxFps 0 and 120) against desktop_ui_host or a real host: presented_fps and picture_latency_ms p50/p95, native presented/s, timings.surface_consume, planeInterval p50/p95, refreshInterval; `pidstat -t -p <pid> 1` per thread; intel_gpu_top or `nvidia-smi dmon`. The UI-thread policy as a separate A/B under scripted Dart load (quality panel open, continuous pan). Occlusion: cover the window 10 s, then another workspace 10 s: no keyframe requests, no 'No video for 5 s' reconnect, receipts continue. Optional glass-to-glass with a 240 fps camera. Record under docs/benchmarks/ with the environment.

name: mac-viewer-enhance
title: macOS viewer: optional GPU enhancement of an enlarged picture (clamped Catmull-Rom plus luma-only sharpening) through a CAMetalLayer, and the shared 'sharpen enlarged picture' preference
design:
Why. A 1920x1080 or 2560x1440 host full-screen on a 3024x1964 to 3456x2234 Retina panel or a 4K/5K external is enlarged 1.2-1.8x bilinearly today, so text is soft. airhand offers luma sharpening with peaks off/low/medium/high = 0/-0.06/-0.1/-0.14 (client/src/lib/enhance.ts:22) and plans the presenter by on-screen size. Off by default, it costs nothing; on, one or two GPU passes at display size (airhand quotes about 0.5 ms on an RTX 4080 laptop; unmeasured on this M6).

Builds on mac-viewer-layer, macOS only:
1. A second presenter mode, active only while enhancement is on and the on-screen pixel size is at least the picture's on both axes (below that the plain YUV layer, as airhand's renderPlan). The on-screen size is the layer bounds converted to the window's root layer times backingScaleFactor, recomputed in layout() and when the mutator transform changes.
2. A CAMetalLayer beside the plain content layer; a switch toggles their isHidden in one main-thread transaction, so the picture never blanks. CAMetalLayer: .bgra8Unorm, sRGB colourspace, framebufferOnly, maximumDrawableCount 3, drawableSize = on-screen pixels.
3. A presenter thread with a newest-wins slot: the feed thread puts the decoded 420v picture there and returns at once. The presenter thread wraps both planes through CVMetalTextureCache (R8, RG8; zero copy); pass 1 converts with the BT.709 limited-range matrix and no transfer conversion (same sRGB look as the plain layer) and upscales with 9-tap Catmull-Rom clamped to the 4 nearest texels into a private intermediate texture (skipped at exactly 1:1); pass 2 applies CAS-style luma-only sharpening with airhand's peaks into the drawable; commit with present. The receipt and timings.present are taken at the scheduled present. It keeps the last picture and redraws when the geometry or level changes. Shaders compile at run time from a source string (MTLDevice.makeLibrary(source:)), so no .metal resource or project-file change.
4. Snapshot keeps using the decoded buffer.
5. Dart: a per-device preference 'Sharpen enlarged picture' (off, low, medium, high; default off) in viewer_prefs.dart and the viewer's Display menu (viewer_menus.dart), sent through `enhance {textureId, level}`, offered only when the texture has a native presenter. linux-plane-scaling reuses the same preference for its plane. Strings in both locales; icons from AppIcons.
6. Docs and CHANGELOG.
verification: Here, from ui/: `flutter gen-l10n` (untranslated stays {}), `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib test tool`, `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos`, `flutter test` (preference and menu). macOS app: `bash scripts/build/pb-mapper-ffi-macos.sh`, then in ui/ `FLUTTER_XCODE_ARCHS=$(uname -m) FLUTTER_XCODE_ONLY_ACTIVE_ARCH=YES bash ../scripts/build/flutter-macos.sh build macos --debug`. CI macos-app, ios-app, flutter-syntax-check.
measurement: On this Mac with mac-viewer-layer's acceptance setup: 1920x1080 and 2560x1440 text clips from desktop_ui_host in a full-screen viewer on the built-in Retina panel and on the G24H2: `xcrun xctrace record --template 'Metal System Trace'` for each pass's GPU time per frame at each level and the change in timings.present against the plain layer; timings.decode and the feed thread's cadence unchanged with enhancement on at 120 fps into 60 Hz (no blocking in nextDrawable); visual A/B at off/low/medium/high from Screenshot.app crops of the same text region; a zoom or resize while the desktop is still must redraw.

name: linux-plane-scaling
title: Linux viewer plane: area-averaged downscaling always, and the shared sharpen-enlarged setting (clamped Catmull-Rom plus luma sharpening) when enlarging
protocol_changes: None on the wire. The runner channel's `place` gains {filter, sharpen}.
design:
Why. Shrinking a 1440p or 4K remote into a window below 0.5x with bilinear and no mipmaps aliases text; enlarging 1080p to a 1440p or 4K full screen is soft. Quality only; nothing changes for bandwidth or latency; it applies only where the plane is active (the Flutter Texture fallback keeps bilinear).

1. Two passes in the plane: YUV to RGBA at the picture's own size (the GL helper's pass), then a scale pass into the placed rect by scale s: s = 1 a 1:1 copy; s < 1, always on, an area filter of up to 3x3 bilinear taps spaced 1/s apart, and below s = 1/3 generate mipmaps of the RGBA texture once per new picture (never per redraw) and sample trilinearly; s > 1 bilinear by default, and when the user picks a level, Catmull-Rom from 9 bilinear taps clamped to the 4 nearest texels plus CAS on luma only with peaks 0/-0.06/-0.1/-0.14 (airhand client/src/lib/enhance.ts:22).
2. Shaders in a GLSL 150 core variant and an ES 1.00/3.00 variant chosen by gdk_gl_context_get_use_es.
3. Dart: the 'Sharpen enlarged picture' preference from mac-viewer-enhance, sent with `place` as {filter, sharpen}; the Display menu offers it while the plane is active.
4. Docs and CHANGELOG.
verification: Here, from ui/: `flutter gen-l10n`, `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib test tool`, `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos`, `flutter test` (the Display-menu setting on Linux targets and the place fields). CI linux-app: `flutter build linux --debug`, `bash scripts/build/check-linux-bundle.sh ui/build/linux/x64/debug/bundle`, `bash scripts/test/linux-desktop-video.sh --software` (shaders compile on llvmpipe in the harness).

name: helper-push
title: Helper protocol: the worker pushes encoded units, fresh-picture notices (with present age) and pointer updates; thread C stops long-polling the pipe
protocol_changes: Helper pipe: bump HELPER_PROTOCOL to one above master's value at merge with both pipe names (.v<n>). Between replies the worker may send tagged records, all deny_unknown_fields: {kind:'unit', generation, video: VideoFormat, pending} followed by its bytes record; {kind:'fresh', presented_ago_us, presented_count}; {kind:'pointer', cursor, shape_serial}. Replies are tagged {kind:'reply', ...Response}; the Video reply gains presented_ago_us: Option<u32> and presented_count: Option<u8> for the submitted picture (serde default, omitted when None). Request gains Stream{on}; Request::Video loses wait_ms (DRAIN_WAIT_MAX_MS goes). Both ends validate: a unit is at most ipc::MAX_FRAME, its generation matches the host's expected context, pending <= 64, the pointer lies inside the display, ages over 1 s are ignored, unknown kinds are rejected. Desktop wire and ALPN unchanged.
design:
Why. Every privileged Windows session ('Turn on remote control' selects Access::Privileged, ui/native/pb_mapper_ffi/src/desktop/host.rs:521-525) pays pipe round trips while active of up to about 500/s, each crossing two pipes and the service relay and costing 3-5 desktop verifications plus AcquireNextFrame in the worker; units arrive 0.3-1 ms late through the drain long-poll; input queues behind that long-poll (0-4 ms); and the helper path gets no present stamps, so the anchored pacer (capture-anchored-pacing) runs on the grid there. Land after win-mf-output-events and win-present-waiter so the worker is event-driven end to end.

1. Worker (oop/server.rs, helper/worker.rs): serve_bound waits on a crate Waiter (platform/windows/waiter.rs) bound to its backend's Waker through PlatformBackend::bind; the exchange task notifies it after each try_send. Each iteration serves queued requests first; then, while Stream{on}: drain finished units and send Unit plus its bytes record (one vectored write_record from helper-pipe-transfer); when the armed source has published a fresh picture, send Fresh{presented_ago_us, presented_count} once per armed present (the age computed just before writing); every 16 ms read the pointer and send Pointer only when it or the shape serial changed. The worker's timer guard follows Stream{on}.
2. Arming: a submitting Video request that finds nothing new leaves the worker's source armed, with the capture thread waiting for a present; no hot_ms.
3. Host (oop/client.rs): one I/O thread owns the current_thread runtime and the NamedPipeClient; call() sends (Request, oneshot) and blocks. The I/O thread demuxes: Reply -> the oneshot; Unit -> a VecDeque bounded at ENCODER_DEPTH + 2 (overflow is a protocol error, NotConnected); Fresh -> a flag, the stamp converted against its receive Instant, and Waker::wake; Pointer -> the cached cursor and serial. bind keeps the Waker; drain_poll and capture_poll -> None; capture_idle_until as MacVideo's; drain_video pops with no pipe call and drops units of another generation; pending = last reported + queued; submitted_picture() returns the Video reply's presented age converted at receipt (this is the helper half of R3-present-anchoring). Input replies keep their post-injection cursor read, which thread C's own-move echo logic needs.
4. Thread C (worker/capture.rs): remove HELPER_DRAIN_WAIT_MAX and DRAIN_WAIT_MAX_MS.
5. platform/synthetic.rs push mode (from capture-anchored-pacing) drives protocol tests over a duplex.
6. Optional, only if the device shows the Fresh-to-submit round trip above about 0.5 ms: let an armed worker submit at the present and push Submitted{presented_ago_us} (needs a thread C hook for a deferred tick).
7. Docs: remote-desktop.md protocol paragraph and history; docs/architecture.md; the user-guide pair (English and Chinese) together; CHANGELOG bullet that the Windows desktop service must be updated (Update installs it).
verification: Here: `cargo fmt --all`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-features`: oop tests over a protocol duplex with PlatformBackend<Synthetic> in push mode: units arrive with no drain request; a stale generation is dropped; pending accounting holds; pointer pushes arrive; an oversize unit and an out-of-display pointer are refused; an age over 1 s is ignored; replies and pushes keep their order; readiness tests for the new number. `cargo test --workspace --all-features`; `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`; `cargo run -p pb-mapper --features desktop --example desktop_loopback`. CI rust-windows-desktop (`cargo clippy -p pb-mapper-desktop -p pb-mapper-ffi --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop -p pb-mapper-ffi --all-features`: the named-pipe I/O thread and the worker loop), nat-traversal.yml.
